title: Docs: expected behavior (H100/L40S/B200) + troubleshooting guide for hardware tuning profiles pack
creator: Talia Benson
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Goal
Create Confluence documentation for the hardware tuning profiles pack that sets clear performance expectations and operational guidance per SKU (H100 / L40S / B200 preview), plus a troubleshooting guide used by SRE/Infra and customer-facing teams during rollout.

Why
Profile changes are intentionally behavior-changing (kernel variants, batching/scheduler heuristics, KV cache/allocator headroom). We need a single source of truth that explains:
- what to expect (latency/throughput/memory trade-offs)
- which signals to monitor
- common failure modes and fast rollback/mitigation actions

Deliverables (Confluence)
1) Expected behavior — H100
- Workload buckets covered by benchmark matrix (short/medium/long prompts; mixed prefill/decode)
- Expected latency/throughput characteristics (p50/p95/p99) and “what moves” when changing key knobs
- Memory headroom assumptions and the defaults used by the profile pack
- Known trade-offs (e.g., higher throughput profiles can increase tail latency under mixed workloads)
- Common failure modes: kernel fallback spikes, queueing inflation, OOM/fragmentation, p99 regressions

2) Expected behavior — L40S
- Differences vs H100 (memory constraints, stability focus)
- Recommended default concurrency/batching caps and why
- OOM/fragmentation prevention guidance and symptoms
- When to pin profile vs when to adjust admission control / traffic shaping

3) Expected behavior — B200 (preview / early access)
- Provisional defaults + explicit caveats (compat gates, driver/CUDA baselines)
- Metrics that must be watched during bring-up (kernel fallback rate, scheduler_queue_ms, OOM signals)
- Rollback guidance (hard gate semantics; require explicit profile_version pin)

4) Troubleshooting guide (cross-SKU)
- “If you see X, check Y” quick table
- Dashboards to use (Runtime Profiles dashboard + key panels)
- Debug bundle fields needed (active profile_id/profile_version/sku; kernel choice counters)
- Triage workflow for:
  a) tail latency regression (queueing vs compute)
  b) elevated kernel fallback rate
  c) OOM / fragmentation / compaction thrash
  d) profile mismatch after model reload / pool migration
- Safe mitigation steps + rollback/kill-switch pointers

Scope notes
- Docs must align with benchmark-lab acceptance thresholds and SRE rollout SLO guardrails.
- Avoid leaking sensitive infra-specific identifiers; keep docs internal to Engineering Confluence.

Links (target pages)
- Confluence: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/expected-behavior-h100
- Confluence: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/expected-behavior-l40s
- Confluence: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/expected-behavior-b200-preview
- Confluence: profiling-playbook/how-to-validate-a-new-hardware-profile (reference)
- Confluence: eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/runtime-profile-observability-dashboard-spec (reference)
- Confluence: eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/profile-rollout-slo-guardrails (reference)

Review requirements
- Runtime: Noah Patel (architecture correctness), Hiro Tanaka (kernel details), Sofia Ivanova (scheduler behavior)
- Applied ML/perf: Claire Dubois (benchmark interpretation), Arjun Desai (quantization interactions called out)
- Infra: Irene Choi (fleet constraints + driver/CUDA assumptions), Vanessa Ortiz (SKU mapping sanity)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (rollout/runbook alignment), Rafael Mendes (rollback steps), Allison Grant (dashboards referenced)

Acceptance criteria
- All 4 pages are published and linked from the profile pack overview.
- Each expected behavior page includes:
  - workload buckets table
  - “watch this” metrics section with exact metric/tag names used by Observability pack
  - known trade-offs + failure modes + mitigations
  - explicit compatibility assumptions (driver/CUDA/MIG policy where applicable)
- Troubleshooting guide includes a 1-page quick triage section that is usable during an incident.
- SRE + Infra sign-off recorded (comment in this ticket with names + date).
comments: 2026-01-16 (Kira Thompson): Draft outline created. Pulling baseline numbers from Jan H100/L40S benchmark runs and will keep the tables qualitative (directional deltas) unless we can confidently quote stable p95/p99 ranges across regions.

2026-01-21 (Allison Grant): Please include the exact metric/tag names we’re shipping (profile_id, sku, kernel_choice, scheduler_queue_ms) and call out cardinality expectations. The dashboard panels assume tags are present on latency histograms too.

2026-01-24 (Irene Choi): For compatibility assumptions: H100 is split (PCIe vs SXM) and some pools still have a driver minor version skew. Please avoid stating a single driver version as “the” baseline; instead document the minimum supported range + how the runtime compatibility gate behaves.

2026-01-29 (Claire Dubois): When describing workload buckets, please tie them to the benchmark matrix naming (e.g., S/M/L prompt bins + mixed workload scenario). Also call out that quantization profiles can shift throughput vs tail in non-linear ways; don’t promise fixed gains if the customer pins a different quant level.

2026-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): Troubleshooting guide needs explicit rollback semantics: what the kill-switch does in Hosted; how Dedicated opt-in works; and how Private customers can pin a known-good profile_version. Also add a “when to page runtime” section with the signals that constitute a P0.

2026-02-07 (Kira Thompson): Pages drafted and shared for review. Added: kernel fallback diagnostic section + queueing vs compute triage flow using traces. Pending: B200 page updates after we confirm driver/CUDA baseline text with Infra.

2026-02-12 (Vanessa Ortiz): L40S page should explicitly call out burst traffic behavior (OOM thresholds) and recommended concurrency caps. We’ve seen fragmentation issues when customers run near max VRAM; advise headroom rather than implying stability at 95–100% utilization.

2026-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Rollback steps look good. Please add a short checklist for on-call: verify active profile in /health, check profile adoption panel, then compare queueing and kernel fallback before rolling back. Also include the auditability note for Dedicated profile pins.
2026-02-22 (Kira Thompson): Incorporated SRE feedback. Marking In Review pending final Infra sign-off on B200 assumptions + one last pass from Hiro on kernel variant wording.
